ROSLYN BRIDGE MCP: AGENT REFERENCE
==================================

MCP server: roslyn
MCP tools: diagnostics, navigate, bulk_navigate, symbols (read-only), edit, lsp
Purpose: C# compiler diagnostics, symbol navigation and semantic edits.
Workspace: the agent session's working directory unless configured otherwise.
Source: saved files on disk. Unsaved editor buffers are not available.

CALL FORMAT
-----------
Each tool takes flat arguments. Examples in this file name the tool first:
diagnostics {"file":"src/Calculator.cs"}

An unknown or missing argument returns invalid_request. For an unknown
argument, the message lists the valid names. An array argument may also be
sent as a JSON string.

Paths are workspace-relative. When no file has the given path, a file name or
a path suffix of whole segments, such as Calculator.cs or Math/Calculator.cs,
also works if it names exactly one workspace file. The response then starts
with a "resolved file: PATH" line. Several matches return ambiguous_file with
up to 20 paths. This applies to file in navigate, bulk_navigate, symbols and
edit, and to diagnostics without glob characters, but not to newName.
Inputs and results use one-based lines and one-based UTF-16 characters, so
returned positions can be reused as inputs. Raw LSP requests keep zero-based
coordinates.

Results are compact text lines. Failed calls start with "error CODE: message"
and set isError. Raw LSP results and capabilities are JSON.
An error, incomplete report or truncated result does not establish success.

CONTENTS
--------
DIAGNOSTICS - File and glob scans, result fields, limits and verification.
SYMBOL NAVIGATION - Definitions, references, call and type hierarchies, hover, symbols, bulk navigation.
SEMANTIC EDITS - Rename and code action preview/apply sequences, stale proposals.
SESSION AND RAW REQUESTS - Status, capabilities, reload and raw requests.

SETUP
-----
If roslyn is absent from the available MCP tools, follow the installation guide:
https://thomas-fazzari.github.io/roslyn-bridge-mcp/getting-started/
This reference describes the tool API.

DIAGNOSTICS
===========

Read errors, warnings and analyzer suggestions from saved C# files.
Start with the files affected by the task. To check that the MCP works,
request diagnostics for one known C# file.

One file:
diagnostics {"file":"src/Calculator.cs"}

Matching files in one project:
diagnostics {"file":"src/Core/**/*.cs","limit":200}

All C# files, only for a requested workspace audit:
diagnostics {}

Use a specific path or narrow glob. Braces check several files in one call:
diagnostics {"file":"src/{Calculator,Program}.cs"}
Omitting file, using "*" or "**/*.cs" selects all C# files. Split large audits
by project or directory.

severity sets the lowest reported severity. The default, warning, reports
errors and warnings. Use information or hint to include analyzer suggestions:
diagnostics {"file":"src/Calculator.cs","severity":"hint"}

Only some codes. Codes match without regard to case, and ids applies before
severity:
diagnostics {"file":"src/Calculator.cs","ids":["CS0246","IDE0005"]}

One line per code, for a large audit:
diagnostics {"file":"src/Core/**/*.cs","summary":true}

RESULT
------
Results are text lines. Each file with diagnostics is followed by one
indented line per diagnostic:
src/Calculator.cs
  12:9 error CS0246 The type or namespace name 'Foo' could not be found

12:9 is the one-based line and character of the start. Pass them unchanged
to the edit tool's code_actions, or pass the code as its diagnostic.
severity is error, warning, information or hint. Clean files are not listed.

A totals line follows the files:
4 files checked, 3 diagnostics in 2 files, 5 below the severity
"below the severity" counts diagnostics left out by the severity filter.
A clean scan reads: 1 file checked, no diagnostics

With ids, the report lists and counts only matching diagnostics, and the
totals line ends with "filtered by ids". A filtered scan with no match reads:
1 file checked, no diagnostics, filtered by ids
That is not a clean file. Other codes may remain.

With summary, each code gets one line instead of one line per diagnostic, sorted
by count and then by code:
CS0246 x12 error src/Calculator.cs:12:9 The type or namespace name 'Foo' could not be found
x12 is the count. The severity, an example location and its message follow. The
totals line still counts diagnostics.

A line starting with "truncated:" means the limit omitted diagnostics.
A line starting with "incomplete:" lists files Roslyn has not attached to a
project. These files get no semantic diagnostics. A file outside every project
stays listed. Check the project file includes it.

LIMITS AND VERIFICATION
-----------------------
limit defaults to 50 and accepts 1 through 250 across the whole response.
It caps returned items, not the files analyzed or the analysis time. With
summary, it caps the code lines.
A truncated result gives the next offset. Send it as offset to skip that many
diagnostics, or code lines with summary. Diagnostics are in file, line and
character order, so pages do not overlap. offset never changes the totals.
A scan accepts at most 1000 files. Narrow the glob if it exceeds this limit.
When the result is truncated, split the selection into narrower requests.
Report the checked scope. A failed, incomplete or truncated response cannot
establish that the workspace is clean.
After writing files yourself, rerun diagnostics on them. An edit applied
through the edit tool already reports the diagnostics of its changed files.
A clean diagnostic report does not replace tests or validate runtime behavior.

After a timeout, narrow the selection. If a single-file retry also times out,
report the failure and stop retrying that request.
Attribute the cause only when logs support it.

SYMBOL NAVIGATION
=================

Name the symbol, or select a position inside it.

By name:
navigate {"action":"references","symbol":"Calculator.Add"}

symbol matches the end of the fully qualified name: Add, Calculator.Add or
MyApp.Math.Calculator.Add. A parameter list selects an overload: Calculator.Add(int, int).
Generic arguments are optional. When Box and Box<T> both exist, Box.Put names
the non-generic one, and Box<T>.Put the generic one. A parameter type also
matches its nullable form: Add(string) selects Add(string?).
A constructor needs its parameter list: Calculator(ILogger).
Partial declarations in one project count as one symbol. Same-named types in
different projects are separate symbols.

If the name matches several symbols, the error ambiguous_symbol lists up to 20
candidates. Send any candidate symbol back unchanged. When candidates share
a name, send the symbol with the candidate's file. When they also share the
file, as an explicit interface implementation and the public member of the
same name, send the candidate's file, line and character. symbol_not_found
means no declaration matched. When symbols with a similar name exist, it lists up to 10
as candidates, one per line. Send one back unchanged. Without candidates, use
the symbols tool to search by partial name.
When no symbol has the member's name and no type matches the container of a
qualified name, as in Nope.Missing, the error says so and names up to 10 types
with a similar name. When the container exists, as in Calculator.Missing, the
error says that the type has no such member and lists its members with a
similar name. Without any, use members to list the type.

By position (file is workspace-relative, line and character are one-based,
character counts UTF-16 code units):
navigate {"action":"definition","file":"src/Calculator.cs","line":12,"character":9}

Replace action with:
type_definition - Find the symbol's type definition.
implementation - Find implementations of an interface or abstract member.
references - Find the references to a symbol. Use definition for its declaration.
reads - Find the references that read a field, property, local, parameter or event.
writes - Find the references that write it.
callers - Find the methods that call this method, with their call sites.
callees - Find the methods this method calls, with the call sites in this file.
supertypes - Find the base types and interfaces of a type.
subtypes - Find the types that derive from or implement a type.
hover - Read type information and documentation.
source - Read the declaration's saved text with its documentation comment.
members - List the members a type declares, across its partial declarations.
  Add inherited: true to also list what its base classes in the workspace pass on.
impact - In one call, gather the references, callers and implementations of a
  member, or the references and subtypes of a type.

source and members also accept a file and a line without a character. They then
use the innermost declaration around that line.

SYMBOL SEARCH
-------------
Document symbols:
symbols {"file":"src/Calculator.cs"}

Workspace symbols:
symbols {"query":"Calculator","limit":50}

For workspace search, omit file. When file is present, query is not used.
Use symbols to locate a declaration, then navigation for semantic relationships.

RESULTS
-------
Results are text lines. Positions are line:character, both one-based, with
UTF-16 characters. Files inside the workspace use relative paths. External and
generated locations keep their absolute URI.

definition, type_definition, implementation and references return one line per file:
src/Foo.cs 42:17 81:9
Location links use the target selection start. limit caps occurrences, not
files. limit defaults to 50 and accepts 1 through 250. A final line starting with
"truncated:" gives the total count and the next offset. Inspect it before claiming
a complete reference or implementation list. No match returns "no locations".
References leave out source-generated code and end with a line counting the
omitted occurrences. Use the lsp tool with action=request to list them.
reads and writes return the lines of references, filtered to the references
that read or write the symbol. x += 1, x++ and out x are writes. A ref argument
is both, except that Volatile.Read and Interlocked.Read only read and
Volatile.Write only writes. A ref argument to any other method that only reads
is still a write. The declaration and its initializer are in neither list.
context, limit, offset and the "truncated:" line work the same, and limit and
offset apply to the filtered list. No match returns "no reads" or "no writes".

callers, callees, supertypes and subtypes return one line per symbol:
src/Consumer.cs:7:26 method MyApp.Consumer.Run(IGreeter)
  calls 7:59
The line gives the declaration position, the kind and then the symbol name.
Send everything after the kind back unchanged as the symbol argument. A result
outside the workspace keeps Roslyn's name. The calls line is present only for
callers and callees. callees lists calls only. A final line counts the
property, field and constant accesses it leaves out.
In every result, a constructor has the kind constructor. An explicit
constructor is named like MyApp.Box.Box(int). A primary constructor has no
declaration of its own, so its line names the type. An empty result reads
"no callers", "no callees", "no supertypes" or "no subtypes". After
"no callers", a line says that reflection or code outside the workspace may
still call the member.

PAGING
------
A truncated result ends with its next offset:
truncated: 300 locations in total, next offset: 50. Raise limit or narrow the query.
Send it as offset to read the next page:
navigate {"action":"references","symbol":"Calculator.Add","limit":50,"offset":50}
offset is the number of results to skip. It never changes the total. navigate,
bulk_navigate and symbols accept it, and bulk_navigate applies it to every
query. A negative offset is an invalid_request error. An offset past the last
result returns "offset past the end:" with the total.
Results keep a fixed order, so pages do not overlap. Locations, related symbols
and members are in file and position order, inherited members after the
type's own. Workspace symbols are ordered by how
well the name matches, then by file and position.

CONTEXT
-------
Add "context":true to see the trimmed source line of each position without
reading the file:
navigate {"action":"references","symbol":"Calculator.Add","context":true}
Each position then gets its own indented line:
src/Foo.cs
  42:17 var sum = calculator.Add(1, 2);
For callers and callees, the lines are the call sites. Callee call sites are in
the requested file. context uses more tokens, so request it only when needed.

source returns a header per declaration, then its text:
src/Calculator.cs:10-14 method MyApp.Calculator.Add(int, int)
A partial type returns one block per part. When a large type does not fit, a
final "truncated:" line counts the omitted lines. Use members, then source on one
member.

members returns the type, then its members grouped by file, relative to the type:
class MyApp.Calculator
src/Calculator.cs
  12:16 method Add(int, int) : int
With inherited: true, each base class in the workspace follows, nearest first:
inherited from MyApp.CalculatorBase
src/CalculatorBase.cs
  8:19 property Name : string
A base class lists every member except private ones, constructors and
finalizers. A private protected member counts as private. An overridden member
appears once. Base types outside the
workspace, such as System.Object, are not listed.
Prefix a member with the type name to send it back, as in MyApp.Calculator.Add(int, int).

impact resolves the symbol once and returns one section per navigation, each
headed by "## ACTION" and shaped like that action's own result. A section that
does not apply reads "## ACTION: none". limit and offset apply to each
section. When the sections do not all fit, the largest ones are left out and
named with their sizes on a final "omitted to fit:" line. Request those alone.

BULK NAVIGATION
---------------
bulk_navigate runs up to 16 independent navigate queries in one call,
concurrently. A query cannot use another query's result. Each query takes the
action, symbol, file, line and character of navigate. context, limit and offset
sit at the top level and apply to every query:
bulk_navigate {"queries":[{"action":"source","symbol":"Calculator.Add"},{"action":"references","symbol":"Calculator.Add"}],"limit":20}

The result has one section per query in request order, headed
"## NUMBER ACTION TARGET". NUMBER starts at 1. TARGET is the symbol, or
file:line:character for a position:
## 2 references Calculator.Add
A query with no result reads "## NUMBER ACTION TARGET: none". A query that fails
shows its "error CODE: message" line in its own section, and the others still
run. A call that times out keeps the finished sections, and the rest report
the error timeout. An impact query lists its sections under "###" headers.
When the sections do not all fit, the largest ones are left out and named with
their sizes on a final "omitted to fit:" line. Request those alone or in a
smaller batch.

Symbols use the same line shape. Document symbols omit the file, give the
declaration end after a dash, as in 5:18-9:2, and indent members under their
container. limit and offset count nested members too. A skipped container leaves
its listed members at its own level. Workspace symbols end with "in CONTAINER".
Hover returns plain text.
Use the lsp tool with action=request for raw LSP locations, full ranges and
location link metadata. Raw results and capabilities are JSON.

SEMANTIC EDITS
==============

Keep edits within the user's requested scope. A preview-only request does not
authorize applying changes. Follow an implementation request through its
authorized edits and validation without adding a separate approval step.

RENAME A SYMBOL
---------------
1. Request a preview at a one-based symbol position:
edit {"action":"rename","symbol":"Calculator.Add","newName":"Compute"}

A symbol name replaces file, line and character, as in SYMBOL NAVIGATION.
code_actions also accepts symbol. A selection still needs file and positions.

2. Read the changed files and edits. Apply the returned proposalId:
edit {"action":"rename","proposalId":"ID_FROM_PREVIEW","apply":true}

When the user already authorized the change, apply in one call without a preview:
edit {"action":"rename","symbol":"Calculator.Add","newName":"Compute","apply":true}

RENAME A FILE
-------------
For a file, newName is the workspace-relative destination:
edit {"action":"rename_file","file":"src/Calculator.cs","newName":"src/Math/Calculator.cs"}

Apply its proposalId with the edit tool, action rename_file and apply true.
This requires Roslyn to advertise file rename support.

FIXES AND REFACTORINGS
----------------------
1. List actions at the diagnostic or selected code:
edit {"action":"code_actions","file":"src/Calculator.cs","line":12,"character":9}

For a selection, also pass endLine and endCharacter, both one-based.
Available actions depend on the installed Roslyn version and loaded project.

To fix a diagnostic, pass its code instead of a position. Add line to pick
an occurrence. The listing then holds only fixes for that diagnostic:
edit {"action":"code_actions","file":"src/Calculator.cs","diagnostic":"IDE0005"}

2. Choose an action from the returned listing. Resolve its preview using the
listing's proposalId and the action's zero-based index:
edit {"action":"code_actions","proposalId":"ID_FROM_LISTING","actionIndex":0}

3. Inspect the preview. Apply its new proposalId:
edit {"action":"code_actions","proposalId":"ID_FROM_PREVIEW","apply":true}

The listing's proposalId with actionIndex and apply true also applies the action,
skipping the preview. So does a fresh request with a position, actionIndex and
apply true, when the user already authorized the change.
Some command-based actions reveal their edits only during execution.

A listing starts with "proposal ID", then one line per action: its zero-based
index, its kind when Roslyn gives one, and its title:
0 quickfix using System.Collections.Generic;
1 quickfix Fix All: Remove unnecessary usings (Document)
2 refactor Introduce parameter for 'x' > into new overload
A fix-all entry fixes every occurrence in the scope in parentheses. A title with
">" is a choice inside a nested action.

Entries under "Suppress or configure issues" are hidden, and a final line
counts them:
35 suppress or configure actions hidden. Set all to list them.
Indexes count hidden entries, so they do not change with "all":true:
edit {"action":"code_actions","file":"src/Calculator.cs","diagnostic":"IDE0005","all":true}

A preview starts with "proposal ID: N files, not applied". Each file operation
follows (change, create, delete, or rename OLD -> NEW), then its excerpts:
@@ 12:9
- int Add(int a, int b)
+ int Compute(int a, int b)
@@ gives the one-based start of the excerpt, followed by "-> LINE:CHARACTER"
when the start differs in the new text. Excerpts keep some unchanged context.
"preview truncated:" marks an incomplete view of the changes.
The preview is limited to 32 000 characters. "truncated: N of M files shown"
marks omitted files, and "command omitted" an omitted command description.
These display limits do not change the edit stored by proposalId.

PROPOSAL LIFETIME AND FAILURES
------------------------------
Proposals expire after five minutes. Reload discards them.
A change to a file the proposal edits, or to a project, props, solution or
editorconfig file, makes it stale. Changes to other source files do not.
On stale_edit, request a new preview against current files. Do not retry the old ID.
After applying, read the errors and warnings that end the result.
After a file creation or rename, the bridge waits for Roslyn to attach the new
file to its project, and reloads Roslyn only if that takes too long.

An application result starts with a status line, then one line per completed
file operation, in order:
applied: 2 files, 2 operations, Roslyn synchronized
change src/Calculator.cs
change src/Program.cs
The status is applied, partially applied or not applied. "Roslyn synchronized"
reports a successful Roslyn refresh. Commands add "command executed" and their
result. On a later failure, the response starts with "error CODE: message" and
"failed step: STEP", with the failed path and operation when known, and then
the receipt. Read both before retrying. After an application failure, the
bridge reloads Roslyn on the next request. Large receipts end with
"truncated: N more operations not shown" or "result omitted".
A successful result ends with the diagnostics of the changed C# files, in the
format of DIAGNOSTICS, for example:
src/Calculator.cs
  12:9 warning CS8603 Possible null reference return.
2 files checked, 1 diagnostic in 1 file
Without that totals line, the check was skipped. Run diagnostics on the
changed files then.

Edits must remain inside the workspace. The bridge rejects symlinks below its
root. Each file replacement is atomic. A failed multi-file operation can leave
partial changes, so inspect the workspace before retrying.
Limits: 256 edited files, 8 MiB per file and 64 MiB total edited content.

SESSION AND RAW REQUESTS
========================

Session status:
lsp {"action":"status"}

Status returns running, loading, workspace and server lines, such as
running: true
loading: false

Roslyn starts loading when the bridge launches if a .sln, .slnx, .slnf or
.csproj file sits at the workspace root or up to two folders below it.
Otherwise it loads on the first language request. If the load outlasts
the startup timeout, the call returns the error loading and the load goes on.
Retry the same call. Status answers at once and reports loading true meanwhile.
While loading, a progress line follows the loading line when Roslyn reports
progress, such as "progress: Loading Calculator.slnx 40%". It has no
percentage when Roslyn reports none. The loading error repeats the progress in
its message.

Server capabilities:
lsp {"action":"capabilities"}

Use capabilities when support for an operation is uncertain.

Reload:
lsp {"action":"reload"}

Reload discards pending proposals. Use it when results remain stale after an
external change, then issue the original query again.

RAW LSP
-------
Prefer the other tools when they cover the operation.
For other methods, pass the LSP method and parameters directly:
lsp {"action":"request","method":"textDocument/hover","parameters":{"textDocument":{"uri":"file:///absolute/workspace/src/Calculator.cs"},"position":{"line":11,"character":8}}}

Replace the example URI with the actual document URI.
Raw LSP positions are zero-based, unlike the other tools.
The bridge reserves lifecycle and document synchronization methods and
workspace/applyEdit.
Unknown methods and workspace/executeCommand require apply true because they
may write files. Use them only within the user's authorized scope.
